name: Status Effects & Crowd Control Loop
description: An end-to-end RPG status and crowd-control loop: ordinary effect-bearing hits enter one Status Effects owner with stable application ids, refresh and stacking, tagged immunities and cleanse, timer-generation expiry, defeat and encounter cleanup, and restore-safe ledgers. Existing hotbar, continuous movement, tactical range, contact attack, elite/boss telegraph, tactical pause, capture, roster, damage, AP, timer, and save owners consume status facts without taking over effect state. Opt-in statusGate behavior rejects or suppresses only the consumer's verb; ignore preserves every legacy pipeline. Original Mirelight effects and scenarios are host-replaceable content, not commercial data.

components.role: sole owner of status instances, stacking, cleanse, immunity, control facts, status timer identity, cleanup, and restore ledgers

definitions.description: A brief bog slick that reduces movement without removing control.
Tethered footing that prevents movement and interrupts attack windups.
A muffling ward that prevents active ability use.
A short full stagger that prevents movement, abilities, and basic attacks.
Stacking defensive pressure; each stack removes one armor.
Independent ember sigils from separate applications.
Up to two ash layers multiply remaining movement speed.
A beneficial two-stack focus that adds attack power.

acceptanceCriteria: Legacy combat.hit effect and effectSeconds payloads still apply with unknownEffectPolicy=legacyAdHoc; existing damage, roster, capture, pause, and telegraph consumers keep their event paths.
A newly entered instance emits effectApplied once; a refresh emits effectRefreshed and a stack increment emits effectStacked, so refreshes cannot create pause or interruption storms.
Refresh keeps the active applicationId while recording the requestedApplicationId; independent effects retain separate application ids and timers.
Stack count never exceeds maxStacks, durationPolicy reset/extend/max/ignore is deterministic, and a capped stack application can refresh duration without adding a stack.
A duplicate applicationId, cleanseId, or removalId is a silent no-op; rejected immunity and capacity requests create no timer, modifier, restriction, or active instance.
Tagged and effect-id immunities reject before state changes; cleanse selects only dispellable matching instances in declared priority or age order.
A timer completion carrying an old generation cannot expire a refreshed or stacked instance; current expiry emits effectExpired and the generic effectRemoved.
With controlRestrictionMode=ignore, hotbar casts, walking, tactical ranges, and automatic contact attacks retain legacy behavior.
With statusGate enabled, a cast restriction produces abilityRejected reason controlRestricted with no resource payment, cooldown, abilityCast, or hit.
A move restriction blocks continuous moveExecuted and reduces tactical reachableTiles to the current tile; moveMultiplier scales speed or movement budget without transferring movement ownership.
An attack restriction empties tactical attackableTiles and suppresses automatic contactMade and hit without spending a ready contact cooldown.
A configured interrupt effect or newly added attack restriction cancels an active elite or boss windup with no committed hit; removing control never commits an attack.
Capture odds refresh on application, refresh, stack, and generic removal, while replayed or restored status events cannot reroll a decided capture attempt.
Defeat, unit removal, and matching elite/boss failure, reset, or completion clear declared transient effects without emitting entityDefeated, loot, XP, or mastery rewards.
Restored active instances, timer generations, and application/cleanse/removal ledgers emit no historical status, control, pause, hit, or capture events.
Save System hears new applications, refreshes, stacks, and generic removals; rejected requests and duplicate replays do not create save-worthy changes.
Removing Status Effects or leaving consumers in ignore mode degrades to the prior combat and movement pack rather than creating a second private restriction ledger.
All effect names, targets, abilities, encounters, values, and scenarios in the Mirelight example are original and replaceable host content.
